lesson.title: The Conditional of Politeness
lesson.subtitle: Infinitive + -ía: me gustaría reservar, ¿podrías ayudarme?, sería fantástico

hook.title: How '-ía' Turns Any Verb into 'Would [Verb]'
hook.content: Because the conditional glues -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían onto the WHOLE infinitive, all three verb families (-ar, -er, -ir) use the exact same endings: hablaría ('I/he would speak'), comería ('I/he would eat'), viviría ('I/he would live'), sería ('it would be', from ser)! And poder drops its e before -ría: podría ('I/he/usted could'), ¿podrías...? ('could you...?')!

pattern.title: Polite Escalation: Quiero → Me Gustaría
pattern.content: While Quiero un café is fine, Me gustaría un café ('I would like a coffee') and ¿Podrías explicarme? ('Could you explain to me?') sound extra gracious and polished.

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: I would like (it would please me)

exercises.target_answer: me gustaría, podría, ¿podrías?, sería fantástico, hablaría
exercises.meaning: I would like (it would please me), I / he / usted could, could you (informal)?, it would be fantastic (ser + -ía), I would speak (hablar + -ía)
exercises.explanation: Full infinitive + -ía creates the conditional across the language.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'It would be fantastic' (from the infinitive ser)?
Assemble: 'I would like to see the house'
exercises.meaning: I would like to see the house

exercises.idea: ask a friend politely: 'Could you speak with my brother?'
cues: speak with my brother → hablar con mi hermano?
idea_parts: speak with my brother → hablar con mi hermano
exercises.meaning: Could you speak with my brother?

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Me gustaría reservar una mesa para dos
exercises.target_answer: Me gustaría reservar una mesa para dos
exercises.meaning: I would like to reserve a table for two
cues: to reserve a table: reservar una mesa
exercises.explanation: Me gustaría reservar una mesa para dos.

summary.outcome: Use me gustaría, podría/podrías, and regular -ía conditionals for polite requests and hypotheticals.

use_example.german: Me gustaría reservar una mesa para dos — ¿podrías confirmar?
use_example.english: I would like to reserve a table for two — could you confirm?

summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([2602] Triggering the Subjunctive): master the opposite-vowel switch (-ar → -e, -er/-ir → -a).

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'I would like to eat here'

gustaría.english_cognate: would please (me gustaría: I would like)
gustaría.english_meaning: would please (conditional: me gustaría = I would like)
gustaría.context_translation: I would like to reserve a table.
gustaría.etymology_derivation: Every Spanish conditional simply glues -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían onto the whole infinitive!

reservar.context_translation: I want to reserve a table.

hablar.english_meaning: to speak, to talk (hablo: I speak)
hablar.etymology_derivation: Latin fabulārī (to converse, tell stories — English fable and fabulous) shifted initial f- to silent h-: hablar!

ver.context_translation: I am going to see it/him today.
ver.etymology_derivation: Pronouns can hook directly onto the tail of the infinitive: verlo ('to see it/him')!

comer.etymology_derivation: Latin com- ('completely') + edere ('to eat', cousin of English edible and eat).

mesa.context_translation: I want to reserve a table.
mesa.etymology_derivation: Latin mēnsa ('table') gave Spanish la mesa — which English borrowed in the American Southwest for a flat-topped 'table' mountain!

café.etymology_derivation: Turkish kahve → Italian caffè → Spanish café. An international word shared across Europe.
